data.narrative:
Q-Factor is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Nir Davidson, Ofer Firstenberg, Yoav Sagi, and Guy Raz, with $24M in total capital raised to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comparables (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression analysis applies to this valuation. Using total raised of $24M as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $60M. Peer-median analysis does not apply: while 6 same-sector peers exist in quantum computing, the narrow peer set yields zero datapoints meeting same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier criteria. Peer comparison on this basis would be unreliable and has been excluded.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to one applicable method, supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), with a median of $60M. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable seed-stage quantum hardware companies in the available dataset and reliance on a single methodological input. Additional data on stage-specific multiples for hardware versus software within quantum computing, or closer peer matches at seed stage, would materially improve confidence in this range.
